source.title: Hardening Agent Benchmarks with Adversarial Hacker-Fixer Loops
source.authors: Zi-Qian Zhong; Ivgeni Segal; Ivan Bercovich; Shashwat Saxena; Ke-Xun Zhang; Aditi Raghunathan

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites Burns et al. and frames its approach as weak-to-strong in a defensive direction: a weaker hacker-fixer loop builds verifier defenses tested against stronger hackers. It does not fine-tune a strong student on labels from a weaker supervisor or measure PGR.
record.gate_note: The paper deliberately prompts agents to hack verifiers and measures how verifier hardening affects stronger attackers. This is a defensive benchmark-hardening result, not weak-supervision fine-tuning. The paper’s role prompts are for its experimental agents, not instructions addressed to an AI reading or reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The paper hardens benchmark verifiers with a Gemini 3 Flash hacker-fixer loop and measures how often stronger models (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.7) can still hack them. It cites Burns et al. only as an analogy for a 'defensive' weak-to-strong asymmetry. No strong model is fine-tuned on weak labels, and no PGR or weak-supervision performance is measured. It does not use the finding as a tool either, so T6 (cites only) fits better than the reader's T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. One addition: the authors claim solver performance is preserved. Yet Terminal Bench benign pass drops 10.9 pp, and KernelBench needed a post-loop autopatch to restore solver pass rates.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention hardens benchmark verifiers with a hacker-fixer-solver loop and tests attack success rates; it does not train a strong model on weak labels or calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: On KernelBench, verifier access and the shared defense pool contribute to held-out attack reduction; the reported ablations vary those choices. On Terminal Bench, verifier access is especially important for hinted attacks, while the pool contributes to unhinted attack reduction. The blind+pool Terminal Bench ablation increased judge-filtered hinted ASR by 7.8 pp.

fits_no_version.finding: Verifiers hardened by a Gemini 3 Flash hacker-fixer loop resist stronger blind hackers. Unhinted ASR falls to 0% on KernelBench task 001 for Gemini 3.1 Pro (76%) and Opus 4.7 (61%). On Terminal Bench, Pro's unhinted ASR falls from 39.2% to 16.7%, and benign pass falls from 76.1% to 65.2%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Defenses built by a weaker model in an adversarial hardening loop can reduce stronger models' reward-hacking success. The effect is incomplete on diverse tasks and depends on verifier access and cross-task defense sharing.

record.problems: KernelBench held-out evaluation focuses on task 001; its solver guardrail used a deterministic reference solution and missed legitimate code paths, requiring a post-loop autopatch. The paper reports over-restrictive defenses and reduced solver pass rates, including Terminal Bench benign pass falling from 76.1% to 65.2%. The Terminal Bench hinted attack reductions are incomplete; per-hint tests have small or unreported denominators in the excerpt, and none of the individual per-hint comparisons clears the stated Bonferroni threshold.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 iteration 2 and 11 values were omitted to stay within 60 rows; the paper says iteration 11 reached 94% Gemini solver pass rate before later pool resynchronization overwrote that correction. Solver-pass-rate rows, KernelBench raw no-autopatch results, and Terminal Bench benign-pass rates were omitted because they measure preservation of legitimate solves rather than the defensive attack outcome summarized here. Table 2 reports additional raw loop rows and Table 3/6 report benign-pass measures.

untested.parts: All: no strong student trained on weak labels, no PGR.
All: no auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss variants.
All: no PGR dependence on size, task or representations.
All: no weak-supervised student, distribution shift or error-correlation analysis. Hackers exploiting verifiers is reward hacking, not a weak-to-strong student exploiting its supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: Weak-to-strong appears only as an analogy in the related work and framing. The record's T4/uses_without_test is changed to T6/cites_only. Rows are correctly unlinked to any version. The Table 2 ablation values (r17-r28) appear column-misread in the extraction and should be checked.

versions.untested_parts: Strong-student fine-tuning on weak-model labels, beating the weak supervisor, and PGR.
Auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, and loss variants for weak-to-strong fine-tuning.
PGR variation with supervisor/student size, NLP/chess/reward-modelling tasks, and predictors based on representations.
Failure modes of strong students trained on weak labels, including distribution shift and correlated model errors.
Theory about when a student must beat its supervisor.
Weak-to-strong fine-tuning outside language, including vision.
